title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — November 23, 2026
summary: Today's threat landscape is marked by active exploitation of cloud identity infrastructure via Microsoft Entra Connect Health (Help Net Security), critical RCE vulnerabilities in Cisco Expressway and legacy ASP.NET libraries (BleepingComputer, The Hacker News), and a major supply-chain payment card breach at software billing giant Cleverbridge (BleepingComputer).

tier1.title: 1. Attackers exploited Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw to access tenant data

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: Help Net Security

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Cloud Identity / Active Exploitation (Cloud Provider Compromise)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Threat actors exploited a vulnerability in the Microsoft Entra Connect Health API to access technical contact email addresses and configuration details across multiple Entra tenants. Entra Connect Health is a core cloud-based monitoring service bridging on-premises identity infrastructure with Microsoft's cloud ecosystem. Exposure of tenant configuration data and technical contacts significantly elevates the risk of targeted spear-phishing and identity infrastructure reconnaissance across enterprise environments.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Review Microsoft notifications for affected Entra tenants, audit Entra Connect Health API logs for unauthorized configuration reads, and alert technical contacts to heightened social engineering risks.

tier2.title: 1. CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Network & Appliance Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) in clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E appliances to execute RPC commands as root. The flaw stems from hard-coded persistent cookies and skipped client certificate validation over the database service, allowing lateral spread across exposed cluster nodes.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Affects Cisco Expressway clusters running X15.5.3 and older; version X14 has no patch available.; CISA has added the flaw to the KEV catalog with an immediate remediation requirement and no available workarounds.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Cisco Expressway-C/E clustering relies on hard-coded persistent cookies and skips client cert validation, so an unauthenticated attacker can run RPC commands as root over the database service.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 2. Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Application Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Threat actors are actively exploiting CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS 9.3), an unsafe deserialization vulnerability in the legacy ASP.NET library Idunno.AntiCsrf (versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta). The flaw enables unauthenticated remote code execution over the network.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Organizations must immediately discontinue use of the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll library and migrate to built-in ASP.NET anti-forgery mechanisms.; Audit web application dependencies across legacy .NET deployments to identify hidden instances of the vulnerable DLL.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Cybersecurity researchers have urged users to discontinue using a legacy ASP.NET anti-CSRF library named Idunno.AntiCsrf following the discovery of a critical vulnerability that has been exploited in the wild.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 3. Google claims last week’s critical VMware bug was under attack in September

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Virtualization & Cloud

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Google Mandiant revealed that CVE-2026-123890, a critical authentication bypass in VMware vCenter patched on November 19, was exploited as a zero-day since September by a China-linked threat actor (UNC5221). The flaw allows unauthorized administrative access to the management console for ESXi hosts and guest VMs.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Patching alone is insufficient for vCenter instances exposed between July and November 2026; full forensic triage is required.; Hunt for unauthorized administrative sessions, anomalous virtual machine snapshots, and persistence mechanisms on vCenter appliances.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Google’s Mandiant unit has claimed that the critical flaw VMware last week revealed in its vCenter product was under attack by a China-linked threat actor which knew of the bug in July and exploited it in September.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Register

tier2.title: 4. Cleverbridge warns hackers stole credit card numbers, CVVs in data breach

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Third-Party & Supply Chain

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: E-commerce billing platform Cleverbridge—which processes payments for major enterprise software vendors including Red Hat, SUSE, Tenable, Veeam, Jamf, and Sony—disclosed a data breach detected on November 4. Attackers accessed internal systems and exfiltrated full payment card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV security codes.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Corporate procurement cards used to purchase software licenses via Cleverbridge storefronts should be rotated immediately.; Monitor corporate credit card statements for unauthorized transactions stemming from exposed CVV data.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: E-commerce platform Cleverbridge is warning that hackers breached its systems and stole customers' payment card information, including credit card numbers and CVV security codes.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 5. Hackers Exploited GL.iNet Cloud Flaw to Install Malware on Routers and KVM Devices

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Hardware & Embedded Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Attackers compromised GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service to push custom malware, backdoors, and reverse shells onto customer travel routers and remote-access KVM hardware. While GL.iNet has patched the cloud vulnerability and blocked the attacker's access route, already-infected devices require local remediation.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Inspect all cloud-connected GL.iNet routers and KVMs for unauthorized cron jobs, reverse shells, and modified firmware.; Perform a full factory reset and firmware re-flash on any device that had GoodCloud remote management enabled.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: GL.iNet has confirmed that hackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to install custom malware on customers' routers and KVM devices, with some affected users reporting backdoors and reverse shells.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 6. Upload2Shell (CVE-2026-125396) is a Ghostscript RCE with public PoC code

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Tracked as CVE-2026-125396 (CVSS 8.5), a use-after-free vulnerability in Ghostscript's Type 1 font loader allows attackers to escape the -dSAFER sandbox via crafted PostScript or PDF files. Public PoC exploit code demonstrates remote code execution via standard file uploads in downstream applications including WordPress Core, Roundcube, Plesk, MediaWiki, and Debian 13 CUPS.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Upgrade Ghostscript to version 10.08.0 immediately across all web servers, mail servers, and print infrastructure.; Block or sanitize PostScript and EPS file uploads at the WAF or application layer if immediate patching is not possible.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A crafted PostScript/PDF triggers a type error, recovers the privileged .forceput operator via a custom error handler, then a use-after-free across save/restore yields RCE.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: #infosec

tier2.title: 7. AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Trigger Unauthorized Payments at Indian Banks and Fintech Firms

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Financial & Threat Intelligence

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: CERT-In issued an advisory warning that threat actors are leveraging AI-assisted attacks against ICT assets across Indian banking, financial services, and technology service providers. The intrusions have directly resulted in unauthorized financial transactions and payment processing manipulations.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Financial institutions should tighten transaction anomaly detection and out-of-band verification for high-value payment routing.; Audit third-party ICT service provider integrations for compromised API credentials and automated exploitation patterns.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: This unsanctioned activity has resulted in unauthorized financial transactions at banking and financial services entities, as well as technology service providers.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 8. Palo Alto Networks confirms two high-severity NGINX vulnerabilities affecting PAN-OS and Panorama

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Network Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Palo Alto Networks confirmed that PAN-OS and Panorama appliances with HTTP/2 enabled are affected by two high-severity NGINX vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 (CVSS 9.2). The flaws allow unauthenticated remote attackers to crash worker processes, corrupt memory, or execute arbitrary code.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Apply Palo Alto Networks and Linux distribution patches for NGINX workers, and restart services to clear vulnerable binaries from memory.; Disable HTTP/2 on exposed management or proxy interfaces as a temporary mitigation if patches cannot be deployed immediately.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, the flaws carry a CVSS score of 9.2 and could allow unauthenticated remote attackers to crash processes or execute code under specific conditions.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: #cve

tier2.title: 9. KEPCO Breach, Aeroméxico Records, Defense Contractor Leak, RCS Zero-Day, Frappe RCE, VPN Access Auction, and Eclipse RaaS

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Threat Intelligence & Dark Web

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), South Korea's primary power utility, confirmed a data breach affecting 1.52 million individuals across its KEPCO ON and SRM systems, exposing registration numbers, bank details, and credit card data. Underground monitoring also surfaced 22 million alleged Aeroméxico records and a claimed 180 TB defense contractor leak.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Energy sector suppliers and partners working with KEPCO should rotate SRM credentials and monitor for supply-chain follow-on attacks.; Monitor dark web intelligence feeds for exposure of corporate credentials tied to the 27-organization VPN access auction.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Attackers accessed the KEPCO ON and SRM systems, stealing registration numbers, bank details, and credit card info.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: SOCRadar

tier2.title: 10. The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of NCIC, the national criminal-justice database

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Government & Critical Infrastructure

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: The FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), the central database used by US law enforcement nationwide to check warrants, stolen property, and background records. The scope of the compromise has not yet been publicly disclosed.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Law enforcement agencies and justice system partners should monitor for anomalous NCIC query patterns or unauthorized credential usage.; Prepare for potential integrity checks or temporary disruptions to connected state and local criminal justice portals.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: NCIC is the system police nationwide use to check warrants and run background checks. It would be the second apparent intrusion at the bureau.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: #infosec

tier2.title: 11. Rackspace Spot breach: leaked credentials let attackers impersonate users on the managed K8s platform

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Cloud & Container Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Rackspace disclosed a security breach of its Spot managed Kubernetes platform on November 17 after leaked credentials allowed attackers to impersonate users for a 10-hour window. The threat actors deployed rogue pods, enumerated nodes and volumes, and exfiltrated cluster secrets including API tokens and cryptographic keys.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Rackspace Spot customers must immediately rotate all Kubernetes cluster secrets, API tokens, and external service credentials stored in affected clusters.; Audit cluster logs from November 17 (12:20–22:00 UTC) for unauthorized pod deployments and lateral movement into connected cloud environments.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: They deployed pods, listed nodes/volumes and read cluster secrets (API tokens, keys). Sessions revoked, keys rotated.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: #infosec

tier2.title: 12. Infected TV boxes in BADBOX 3.0 rent out their owners’ home internet

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Malware & Botnets

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: HUMAN's Satori team disrupted BADBOX 3.0, a massive botnet operating primarily from pre-infected, low-cost Android TV boxes that generated 40 billion ad bid requests daily (over 4% of global connected TV traffic). Beyond hidden video ad fraud, the malware turns residential networks into proxyjacking exit nodes for cybercriminal traffic.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Block unmanaged Android TV and off-brand streaming devices from connecting to corporate or sensitive work-from-home VLANs.; Update threat intelligence blocklists with BADBOX 3.0 C2 domains and monitor for anomalous residential proxy traffic.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: HUMAN’s Satori Threat Intelligence and Research Team has disrupted BADBOX 3.0, an operation run mainly from infected low-cost TV boxes that generated roughly 40 billion ad bid requests a day at its peak.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Help Net Security

tier2.title: 13. Google’s semantic governance policies can block an AI agent’s tool call before it runs

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: AI Security & Architecture

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Google introduced semantic governance policies in Preview on the Gemini platform, combined with its donation of Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF. The architecture places an external checkpoint at an enforcement gateway to evaluate and block proposed AI agent tool calls that deviate from user intent or violate enterprise policy prior to execution.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Enforce AI agent security boundaries outside the model runtime using external policy gateways rather than relying on system prompts.; Use sandboxing technologies like gVisor and Agent Substrate to isolate agent compute from persistent state.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Semantic governance policies, in Preview on the Gemini platform, look at each tool call the agent’s model proposes and block it before it runs if the call doesn’t match the user’s request or breaks a company rule.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Help Net Security

tier2.title: 14. Project Chaperone: A Rule-Enforcing Harness for Proactive Assessment and Prevention of AI Agent Misconduct

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: AI Security & Governance

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Project Chaperone is a newly released open-source runtime harness designed to constrain AI agents using explicit data-flow, action, output, and network policy checks before and during execution. Alongside Xalgorix—an open-source AI pentesting tool that uses a secondary agent to re-exploit and verify findings—defenders are gaining deterministic controls over agentic workflows.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Implement deterministic data-flow and network rules around autonomous agents to prevent data exfiltration and unauthorized tool execution.; Adopt dual-agent verification patterns in automated security testing to eliminate false positives before alerting human analysts.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Practical agent safety needs enforceable runtime boundaries, not just instructions.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: TLDR data

tier2.title: 15. CVE-2026-134817: an argument injection flaw in Flux159's mcp-server-kubernetes

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Cloud & AI Infrastructure

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: An argument injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-134817) in Flux159's mcp-server-kubernetes (versions prior to 4.2.0) allows remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients to inject arbitrary kubectl flags and read local files on the server host. Separately, CVE-2026-133968 was disclosed as an AI-discovered zero-day path traversal flaw in the MONAI Label medical imaging server.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Upgrade mcp-server-kubernetes to version 4.2.0 and restrict MCP server network exposure to trusted orchestrators.; Healthcare organizations using MONAI Label should apply patches for CVE-2026-133968 and restrict unauthenticated API access.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: An argument injection flaw in Flux159's mcp-server-kubernetes lets remote MCP clients inject kubectl flags and read files on the server host.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: #infosec

tier2.title: 16. A Mongoose heap overflow rated CVSS 9.8 enables pre-auth remote code execution

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: IoT & Embedded Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: A critical heap overflow in the Mongoose MIP TCP/IP stack enables pre-authentication remote code execution (CVSS 9.8), patched in Mongoose 7.24 alongside six other flaws. Additionally, CVE-2026-129975 (a critical double-free in GPGME affecting Gpg4win, mail clients, and Samba) and CVE-2026-134624 (an N-able MailAssure internal network scanning flaw via LDAP sync) require immediate patching.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Update embedded projects using Mongoose to version 7.24, upgrade GPGME to 2.3.1, and patch N-able MailAssure to 20261121.1943+.; Ensure embedded IoT management interfaces and LDAP synchronization endpoints are isolated from untrusted network segments.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A Mongoose heap overflow rated CVSS 9.8 enables pre-auth remote code execution in the MIP TCP/IP stack. Mongoose 7.24 fixes it and six other flaws.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: #infosec

tier2.title: 17. Signal blocks AI assistants from peeking at your private messages

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Endpoint & Privacy

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Signal rolled out client protections to prevent OS-level AI assistants—specifically Apple's Siri Onscreen Awareness in iOS 27 and Google Gemini on Android—from capturing screen content or reading user conversations. Elsewhere in client security, Microsoft Edge is testing a Canary 'Lockdown Mode' that disables WebGL and WebGPU to eliminate roughly 60% of browser GPU privilege escalation exploits.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Enterprise mobile security teams should evaluate how OS-level screen-reading AI assistants in iOS 27 and Android interact with confidential corporate messaging apps.; Consider testing Microsoft Edge Lockdown Mode for high-risk executive and administrator endpoints to reduce browser GPU attack surface.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Siri Onscreen Awareness (iOS 27) and Gemini Intelligence on Android can no longer capture Signal screen content, and screenshots are blocked on iOS 27.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Help Net Security

tier2.title: 18. Four bytes, no pairing, no PIN: any Bluetooth device in range could apply Elecbrakes trailer brakes

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: OT, ICS & Physical Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Researchers discovered that Elecbrakes Bluetooth trailer brake controllers required pairing for firmware updates but left brake control unauthenticated, allowing any device in range to lock trailer brakes at full force via a 4-byte command. In industrial OT news, CERT@VDE published advisories for WAGO controllers (CVE-2026-80466, CVE-2026-88850), Wiesemann & Theis PHP2Shell RCE (CVE-2026-109618), and unauthenticated ifm cameras (CVE-2026-121613).

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Apply manual firmware updates to Elecbrakes EB2 and VM1 units immediately; monitor for upcoming fixes for the ELBC 2000 model.; Review CERT@VDE advisories VDE-2026-135, VDE-2026-096, and VDE-2026-148 to patch affected WAGO, Wiesemann & Theis, and ifm industrial devices.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Four bytes, no pairing, no PIN: any Bluetooth device in range could apply Elecbrakes trailer brakes at any force, and get a notification confirming it.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: #infosec
